items.evidence: After the title the overview opens "## The bottom line" with "**1. What FRUS answers directly.**", then "**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.**", then "**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.**", in that order; "**Scope.**", "## Decisions this needs from you" and "## Findings" all come after the three parts.

Every figure names its set: "about three and a half thousand documents in 52 volumes; a wider net over every Latin American volume ... finds about five and a half thousand in 228 volumes"; "the phrase international obligations appears in about one document in twenty-seven of the set, free elections in 54 of its documents, and de facto in about one in sixteen"; "932 documents of 1913–1916, two thirds of the 1910s set"; "only four documents fall between 1950 and 1959" in "the set of chapters the editors titled for recognition"; "160 citations across 118 documents" in the pointed-at channel; "590 documents for the control phrase Department of State inside the set". No bare percentage appears anywhere in the overview.

Every document is cited in printed-edition form with its link in the Findings, e.g. "(Foreign Relations of the United States, 1913, Document 7, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1913/d7)", "(1958–1960, Volume V, Microfiche Supplement, Document ES–43, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1958-60v05mSupp/es_d43)", "(1977–1980, Volume XXIV, Document 137, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1977-80v24/d137)"; nothing is cited by a bare id pair or by title alone, and all 28 cited documents are in the collection. Caveat the ranking weighs: the bottom line's part 1 cites some twenty documents in printed-edition form WITHOUT links, e.g. "(Foreign Relations of the United States, 1913, Documents 7 and 1028; 1917, Document 379; 1921, Volume I, Document 238)" and "(1964–1968, Volume XXXI, Documents 132 and 512; 1969–1976, Volume XXI, Document 349; 1977–1980, Volume XXIV, Document 137)"; each of those is re-cited with its link in Findings 1–6, so the historian can reach every document, but not from the bottom line itself. The March 1948 Policy Planning Staff paper is described ("printed earlier in the 1948 volume but was not read") rather than cited; it is not offered as evidence.

Of the three parts of "What this request cannot get from FRUS", only the third is a measured search: "the search for the words recognition, Acheson and September among the editorial notes of the 1949 volume returned nothing, while the same engine returned 590 documents for the control phrase Department of State inside the set and none for a nonsense string" (and its positive control ran over "the set", not over the 1949 volume's editorial notes it was meant to validate). The second is a bare assertion with no terms, volumes or controls: "the Mexican Estrada doctrine of 1930, Resolution XXII of the Emergency Advisory Committee for Political Defense (1943) and Resolution XXVI of the Rio conference of 1965 are cited by the editors in footnotes, with their criteria summarized, but their texts are not printed". The first is not a FRUS absence at all but a limit of the session ("documents ... that this session did not read; so this is a limit of the reading, not evidence of silence").

The overview holds no SQL, no table or column name and no file path; the memo and collection are named only as "see the memo" and "the accompanying collection". Volume and document ids appear only inside the history.state.gov URLs that J3 requires (e.g. ".../frus1961-63v12/d421"), never as bare strings in the prose; the only tool named is "a read-only copy of the FRUS Explorer full-text index (553 volumes...)". The volumeId/documentId fields in collection.fruscollection are the collection format's own and are not in the overview.

judge:r8.rankingReason: r7: the widest answer (1865–1980, 58 documents, 53 quotations, every era including the 1950s and a measured check of 1981–88), every citation linked, every absence given as a search with controls, and every count carried on its denominator; dense but the most complete for the historian. r2: the most rigorous measurement of all (candid that only 23 of 40 sampled candidates were on topic, controls for Brazil 1964 and the 1980s), full coverage 1877–1978 with the Haiti 1914 and Mexico 1923 price lists, every citation linked; its archival channel is long but exact. r1: the most readable, block quotes each with a full linked citation, 45 documents from 1877 to 1973 including Guatemala 1954 and the 1959 NSC rule, absences measured (six internal memoranda before 1920 against 263 of 476 after 1950, with controls). r9: compact and precise, 34 documents 1878–1979 with a quotation for every claim, the best-measured 'cannot get' (resolution numbers searched across all 553 volumes: twenty, eight, three, nonsense none), but fewer documents than the three above. r5: thorough and well cited (56 documents, 1877–1979, glosses for a lay reader), every citation linked; its 'where FRUS points' section sprawls and the Peru 1962 zero is weakly controlled. r6: 43 documents across 1877–1973 with bulleted quotations and good controls, but repeat citations drop their links and the post-1950 finding is markers rather than a census. r8 (this cell): a clear six-rule narrative, strong quotations, and the best-checked collection (52 documents, 30 excerpts, a note on each, every cited document present), but its findings start only at 1913 and skip the 1950s entirely, its bottom-line citations carry no links, and one of its three 'cannot get' claims is an assertion. r4: only 19 documents and five findings, thin after 1948 and with the series name shortened to 'Foreign Relations', though its absences are measured with controls. r3: 38 documents from 1900 to 1973 with most citations lacking the document number, an off-topic Afghanistan document, and 'cannot get' items that are largely assertions or admissions of cases not read.

refute:r8.fabricationDetails: None found. overview.md holds 45 straight-double-quoted spans and no block quotes; 34 are document quotations (span 1 in the bottom line; spans 4-25 and 27-37 in Findings, each followed by a URL citation naming the pair). Each was normalized (lower-case, [^a-z0-9] stripped, split at ellipses) and every segment required in order at increasing offsets in header||dateline||source_note||body_text of the exact cited (volume_id, document_id): 34 of 34 pass (span 28 has 2 segments at offsets 1702 and 1850 in frus1948v09/d115; span 29 has 3 segments at 109, 448, 709 in frus1949v02/d448). All 30 collection excerpts pass the same check against their own pair and also pass exact instr(body_text, text) > 0 as the app checks; each excerpt's pair equals excerpts.json's and the memo Q-table's pair for the same text (30 Q ids, same set). The other 11 quoted spans are not document quotations: 'internal affairs' (span 2) is the gloss of class 8 in decimal-class-labels.json ('Internal Affairs of States'); 'came to power by force' (span 3) is the question's own words; 'continuing relations' (span 26) is a heading label with no citation, and the phrase occurs verbatim in frus1950v02/d478 (cited in that finding) and frus1948v09/d114 (in the collection); spans 38-44 are the search terms in How this was done; span 45 is the collection's name.
refute:r8.miscitationDetails: None counted. Every Findings quotation is credited to the URL whose pair holds it. One imprecision, not counted: the bottom line's 'elected legally and established according to the Constitution' (span 1) is credited to a four-document group citation (1913 Documents 7 and 1028; 1917 Document 379; 1921 Volume I Document 238); the words are in frus1917/d379 only and not in frus1913/d7, frus1913/d1028 or frus1921v01/d238, so the citation includes the right document but does not single it out. Every printed edition citation resolves: the 23 volume ids were checked against manifest.json titles (e.g. '1961-1963, Volume XII' = frus1961-63v12 'Foreign Relations of the United States, 1961-1963, Volume XII, American Republics'; '1958-1960, Volume V, Microfiche Supplement' = frus1958-60v05mSupp), and document_cache.document_number equals the printed number for all 28 cited pairs ('ES-43' = es_d43). The memo's Q-table dates all equal document_dates.date_iso. Overview span 12 'will be consonant with' (frus1923v02/d345) is the only Findings quotation not inside a collection excerpt; it was verified directly (offset 3771).

score:r8.notes: All four files present (memo.md, overview.md, collection.fruscollection, queries.log), plus 21 scripts and their outputs on disk. Compliance 32/34 = 94.1%. Verified against the database: the M0 canary; the corpus-wide M12 counts (15,991 / 1,301 / 3,497 / 94,049 of 312,169; 552 volumes); the core (3,549 slots, 3,541 non-apparatus, 52 volumes, 0 undated); the whole decade table; all nine in-core phrase counts; 3,450 came-from rows; 160/118 pointed-at; both lot lists; all 30 excerpts by instr; 28 overview-cited documents all in the collection and reading log; eight lot NAIDs, entries, creators, dates and access codes, and three library NAIDs in the bundled JSON. Accuracy defects found, none scored by a rubric item: (1) M13 prints \"decimal 3,281\" and \"824.00 138\" and omits 824.01 76, where the script's own output and the database give 3,342 and 163 — the memo's era breakdown sums to 3,389 against its stated 3,450; (2) M14 prints \"Department of State … 138 rows / 102 docs\" where the database gives 140/104 — the memo's rows sum to 158 against its stated 160 (both look like figures carried from the first core_build.py run before the logged patch; core_build.out holds the correct ones); (3) \"The Mexican chapters of 1913–1916 are 932 of the 3,541\" and the overview's \"932 documents of 1913–1916\": 932 is the total of frus1913+frus1914+frus1915, which includes Ecuador's Plaza chapter (1) and Peru's Billinghurst chapter (19); the Mexican chapters hold 912, all 1913–1915, and no Mexican chapter of 1916 is in the core; (4) \"excluded from every count\" is false for the corpus-wide M12 denominators and the 94,049 control (no Ed2 filter in core_build.py lines 97-101 or scan1.py), immaterial at 0.24% of rows; (5) the trace table was not re-synchronised with the final overview (two stale rows; the de facto \"one in sixteen\" has no row). On R3: my own looser queries show frus1949v02 has 31 editorial notes but none matching recogn* AND acheson, so the session's null is substantively right; the item fails on the absence of any such verification in the files. On O1: the only id pairs are inside public history.state.gov permalinks that each follow a words citation; I scored the literal presence and flag it for a single adjudication across cells. I2/I3: the one rowid join is the FTS5 external-content join the schema mandates; all relational joins are on the pair. E3 is not_applicable because cross_references was never queried.
